html:
The British Mandate of Mesopotamia was British rule over what became Iraq, from 1920 to 1932, under a mandate of the League of Nations. The map shows it from 1920 to 1938.

British and Indian troops took the Ottoman provinces of Basra, Baghdad and Mosul during the First World War. In 1920 a large uprising, the Iraqi revolt, cost Britain dearly. Britain chose to rule more cheaply through a local king. In 1921 it put Faisal, the Hashemite leader of the Arab Revolt who had just been expelled from Syria by the French, on the throne of Iraq. British advisers and the Royal Air Force kept real control.

Oil was struck near Kirkuk in 1927, and the foreign-owned Iraq Petroleum Company took the profits. In 1932 Iraq became formally independent, the first mandate to do so, but Britain kept air bases and influence there.
